minutes.headline: Sewer Commission voted to cut school grease trap pumping to once a year, internal traps included, starting August.
minutes.summary: The commission heard a school facilities request to reduce grease trap pumping, then amended and approved it to cover all traps. It also reviewed an ARPA request to the select board built on increased pump flows from COVID, a pending engineering proposal, a new additional-flow application and fee, and a tight budget with high delinquency.

Closing public comment: none from the public; a member offered condolences to Jane and her family.

votes.outcome: amended before the vote; see next

votes.motion: Amend the motion to include all grease traps, including internal ones, on a yearly pumping schedule; then roll call vote on the amended motion.
votes.outcome: roll call taken at ~866; individual votes not clearly captioned, but the commission proceeded as adopted

votes.motion: Adopt the application for additional flow and the fees as outlined on the form.
votes.outcome: passed (roll call; chair said 'it is passed')

A proposal for a flow study; the commission tabled it to next meeting and to fiscal 24 funds because the budget is tight.
New application sets a per-bedroom charge for residential and a per-gallon-per-day charge for commercial, under existing regulations.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to pump the schools' grease traps once a year starting August 2023, after amending the request to cover internal traps too.
The commission adopted a new application and fee schedule for additional sewer flow, under existing regulations.
The commission agreed to send the select board an ARPA funding request with a line chart and an added paragraph.
A proposed engineering flow study was tabled to the next meeting because the budget is tight.
The manager reported high delinquency and revenue below forecast, with a small deficit likely to be covered from retained earnings.

why_it_matters: Sewer users pay for the system through charges and betterments, so a shortfall in collections and a request for ARPA money bear on future rates and on what the town's general funds are asked to cover.
The new additional-flow fee sets what a new bedroom or commercial connection pays to join the system.
